corpusSummary: A 2026 collection of social-science papers on large language models examining human–AI interaction, education, health, policy, and methodological use. It highlights trust, embodiment, and anthropomorphism, alongside AI-driven research methods, governance, and ethics. The corpus exposes both practical opportunities for AI-enabled learning and decision support, and warnings about reliability, bias, mis/ misinformation, and environmental costs.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction and embodiment dynamics
themes.description: Research explores perceived humanness vs. empathy, trust, disclosure, and the effects of AI device embodiment on well‑being, adoption, and social behavior.

themes.name: AI as a methodological tool for social science
themes.description: A suite of studies uses LLMs for coding, framing codebooks, data extraction, cross-domain transfer, simulations, and governance frameworks to augment research practice.

themes.name: AI in education and health domains
themes.description: Work examines AI-enabled learning, AI tutoring, educational analytics, and AI-generated health information and counseling, with attention to motivation, anxiety, and accessibility.

themes.name: Equity, governance, and ethics of AI deployment
themes.description: Articles propose equity-first governance, fairness evaluations, and critical perspectives on AI's societal impacts, assessment practices, and policy integration.

emergingKeywords: AI adoption in organizations and policy
